ui.endcard.fragments: Memories you managed to keep: {count} of 13
whisper.W02: It’s me. Do you remember me?
whisper.W05: Come inside. It’s cold out here.
whisper.W07: Look at me... please look at me.
whisper.W08: My name is --- ... my name is ---...
monolog.L06: What time is it? What day?
monolog.L13: This room... isn’t here. I must have been here before.
monolog.L14: I want to leave, but the door always returns to the same place.
monolog.L15: I’m turning, but I’m not moving forward.
monolog.L16: I can’t control my body. But I know I am here.
monolog.L17: I search for a way, but there is none. I just... am.
monolog.L18: I forgot my name. But I remember the light.
fragment.F0: Warm tea. Someone always set it on this table.
fragment.F1: Warm tea on a quiet morning. Someone always set it here.
fragment.F2: The wool is rough, but warm. Someone knitted it for me... who?
fragment.F3: I know this tune. I used to hum it before sleep.
fragment.F4: We were laughing in this photo. Those faces must be people I love.
fragment.F5: My glasses. Where did I leave them? Ah, here.
fragment.F6: That door was always open to me. Once.
fragment.F7: The pages are full of my handwriting. I can’t read it anymore.
fragment.F8: Tick, tick, tick. What time is it? What day?
fragment.F9: The smell of fried shallots. Someone is calling me to eat.
fragment.F10: Rain. A hand holding mine. Warm.
fragment.F11: I want to write my name. N... a... me...
fragment.F12: This sound once meant coming home.
ending.title: NOOR
ending.e6: I forgot my name. But I remember the light.
ending.e7: They are still here. They just no longer know that it's you.
education.title: About Alzheimer's
education.body: Alzheimer's is not just forgetfulness. It is a progressive brain disease that changes perception, emotion, and daily life. A person may not recognize those closest to them. Stay calm, introduce yourself, and do not argue harshly.
education.caregiver: Caregivers need support too. No one should face this alone.
